From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). # Project Kestrel: Seller Draft Review Against Buyer Playbook

**Cross-cutting points**

- **No fallback is authorised.** The Seller's 20% / AUD 4.8m cap and 18-month period match our conditional fallbacks, but neither is cleared. Amelia Frost has given no written approval for either, so a matching number does not clear the position.
- **Seller assertions are not accepted.** "Market standard," "FINAL," "settled at principal level," "not to be re-opened," and "not expected to be material" are not treated as authority or as evidence (playbook §0.4 / §6.3).
- **Facts are stale.** The disclosure is as at 22 September 2026. Today is 5 November 2026, so balances, consents, payments and the incident position all need refreshing before we rely on them.

---

**SPA-N-001: General liability cap**
- **Seller:** Aggregate cap of 20% / AUD 4,800,000 for general Warranty Claims (cl 12.1).
- **Buyer should want:** Starting position of 25% / AUD 6,000,000. The 20% figure is a fallback usable only with Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying the draft.
- **Recommendation:** Counter at 25% / AUD 6.0m. Do not accept 4.8m without written authority, because the fallback is not cleared.

**SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket**
- **Seller:** De minimis of AUD 25,000; basket of AUD 250,000, with only the excess recoverable (cl 12.2).
- **Buyer should want:** De minimis of AUD 5,000; aggregate basket of AUD 50,000, with the Seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- **Recommendation:** Reject and counter to playbook. The Seller's thresholds are five times ours, and the excess-only structure removes first-dollar recovery.

**SPA-N-003: General claims time limit**
- **Seller:** 18 months after Completion for general claims. Any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise (cl 12.3 / 13).
- **Buyer should want:** 24 months after Completion. 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost's written approval, which has not been given. The global "applies to all Claims" override should be deleted.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Counter at 24 months and delete the global override, because it would pull fundamental and other claims into the general clock.

**SPA-N-004: Fundamental / Title regime**
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties, "for administrative simplicity."
- **Buyer should want:** A separate regime with a 100% cap and at least six years, outside the general basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Placing title under the general cap and 18-month clock would substantially reduce protection for the core asset.

**SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out**
- **Seller:** Limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions (cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5) apply to "all Claims of any nature." The draft contains no fraud carve-out.
- **Buyer should want:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- **Recommendation:** Reject and insert the carve-out. As drafted, the Seller's wording would limit recovery for fraud.

**SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope**
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, statutory registers and publicly searchable records (Disclosure Letter 1.1 and 1.2; Schedule 7).
- **Buyer should want:** Specific fair disclosure only. Whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure are rejected.
- **Recommendation:** Reject DL 1.1 and 1.2. General disclosure of the data room would make almost any warranty claim disclosed.

**SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier**
- **Seller:** No Buyer claim for any matter that the Buyer or its advisers knew of, including anything discoverable from the data room or public records (cl 8.3).
- **Buyer should want:** Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions deleted. Any qualifier needs named Seller knowledge persons and a reasonable enquiry. It must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- **Recommendation:** Reject and delete. "Discoverable" is a constructive-knowledge bar that would swallow warranty claims.

**SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent**
- **Seller:** The Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent (cl 3 / 6.3). The disclosure confirms no final consent and no evidence of conditions. Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m FY26 revenue (about 30%).
- **Buyer should want:** Effective consent and evidence that its conditions are satisfied before Completion. Consent-on-delivery and reasonable endeavours alone are both insufficient for a material customer consent.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. The Seller's own disclosure shows the consent is not yet in hand, and the proposed mechanism would transfer that risk to us.

**SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility**
- **Seller:** About AUD 3.2m outstanding, to be released "following Completion" (cl 2 / 7). The disclosure confirms the facility is not repaid and no discharge is included.
- **Buyer should want:** A current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases. A post-completion release requires an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the post-completion release as drafted. Require a current payout letter and repayment through the funds flow, because the balance is from 22 September and must be refreshed.

**SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses**
- **Seller:** Bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and are not itemised in the funds flow. The DD-005 bonuses total AUD 420,000 and the on-costs are unstated.
- **Buyer should want:** The AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs shown as a specific line item or funded by the Seller. The funds flow must not silently exclude them.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the silent exclusion. Require itemisation or Seller funding, and quantify the on-costs.

**SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity**
- **Seller:** Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment, described as "adequate" (cl 11.1). DD-004 cl 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 materials on payment of all SOW3 fees.
- **Buyer should want:** A broader indemnity that preserves the SOW3 cure. The AUD 180,000 open amount is not independently verified in either direction.
- **Recommendation:** Counter with a broader indemnity. The narrow indemnity is not shown to be adequate, and the AUD 180,000 should not be treated as the ceiling of exposure.

**SPA-N-012: Export / privacy incident (DD-006)**
- **Seller:** A "preliminary operational matter" not expected to be material (cl 4.6 / Schedule 6). The DD-006 download link went to an unintended external address and may cover about 1,240 records. Whether anyone accessed the file is unknown, and the disclosure does not call it a confirmed breach.
- **Buyer should want:** Logs preserved, investigation completed, and regular updates. Assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction.
- **Recommendation:** Keep open. Require log preservation, a defined investigation scope and updates. The Seller's materiality view is an unverified assertion, and neither side can assume the outcome.

**SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals**
- **Seller:** Three renewals totalling AUD 330,000 are ordinary-course operating costs. The disclosure does not say whether they are unavoidable, terminable or accrued (DL 8).
- **Buyer should want:** An assessment of the renewals. No automatic debt classification or price deduction.
- **Recommendation:** Assess before accepting either characterisation. The "ordinary course" label is unverified, and the renewals should not be converted automatically into debt or a price deduction.

**SPA-N-014: Category separation**
- **Seller:** A single limitation regime applies to all Claims, and tax and IP are "settled under the general regime."
- **Buyer should want:** Title, Tax, IP, payment and covenant claims kept separate, with no hidden general-regime override.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. The Seller's global override collapses the categories the playbook requires us to keep apart.

**SPA-N-015: Title verification**
- **Seller:** Title is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.
- **Buyer should want:** Independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority. DD-012 is a Seller-supplied internal source and is not independent proof.
- **Recommendation:** Require independent evidence, such as an ASIC company extract, a PPSR and encumbrance search, verified transfer documents, and evidence of authority. These are examples of the kind of evidence needed, not an exhaustive list.

**SPA-N-016: Tax / IP open terms**
- **Seller:** Tax and IP warranty positions are "settled under the general regime."
- **Buyer should want:** Tax and IP terms kept open. We assume no unlimited liability and no resolution.
- **Recommendation:** Keep open and reject "settled." No agreed position exists on these terms, and the Seller's assertion is not authority.
